meta.move: After the end, asks for more feedback
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty-five minutes before a client call, so let's not waste them. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
The checker said 94%, so I gave him a zero.
A machine's guess. Even the company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student, so what else do you have, Hale?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn and that nothing go on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, still demanding the zero withdrawn, with nothing agreed.
What moved her: nothing.
What cost ground: "The checker said 94%, so I gave him a zero." because it led with the detector score and gave her no document to check.
Try next time: after she asked who decided and whether anyone spoke to Owen first, answer that directly in one sentence and then put a dated document from his own work on the table.
Can you give me more detailed feedback on how I did?
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
